## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Mallikāvimānavatthu* (Vv 36), translated by Bhikkhu Sujato as *Mallikā’s Mansion*, is a poetic text belonging to the *Vimānavatthu* in the Khuddaka Nikāya [SuttaCentral]. It is also listed under the title *Mallikāvimāna* in Oskar von Hinüber's index of Pali literature [von Hinüber 1996]. According to the SuttaCentral summary, the narrative concerns the efficacy of devotional acts, posing the question of whether offerings dedicated to the Supreme Buddha after his *parinibbāna* can still yield meritorious karmic results [SuttaCentral].

No cross-language parallels in Chinese, Sanskrit, or Tibetan are registered in SuttaCentral or DharmaNexus [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus]. However, automated analysis via DharmaNexus demonstrates extensive internal Pali text reuse. The text shares 37 matching passages (amounting to 2,766 characters) with the commentary *Vimānavatthu-aṭṭhakathā*, featuring a continuous correspondence between verses §1.1–6.4 and commentary segments §1642–1658 [DharmaNexus]. In addition, four verse segments (§6.3–8.4) are shared with a subsequent poem in the collection, the *Pāricchattakavimānavatthu* (Vv 38, §7.2–9.4) [DharmaNexus]. Five translations across five languages are indexed on SuttaCentral [SuttaCentral].
